purpose: Characterize whether the English C.2 build_ratio 1.8689× (single CREATE INDEX wall clock) is a stable property of the representation or a single-run artifact. Design §9 diagnostic attachment to an escalation; does not replace or flip the gate.

c2_reference.note: C.2 measured one CREATE INDEX per system. This profile does not overwrite those fields.

environment.gucs: defaults plus listen_addresses=127.0.0.1, unix_socket_directories under /tmp/stn4-c2-profile/sockets, shared_buffers=128MB (initdb default)

protocol.interleave: A/B repetition with A=stn4_multi then B=stn3_single in every pair (see order_balance: not counterbalanced)

create_index_sql.stn4_multi: CREATE INDEX idx ON documents USING stannum (title, body)
create_index_sql.stn3_single: CREATE INDEX idx ON documents USING stannum (concat)

protocol.concat_note: Matches C.2 fragment create_index_sql exactly: column (concat), not a functional expression index. concat is GENERATED ALWAYS AS (title || ' ' || body) STORED, same as benchmarks/stn3_fielded_poc.py load_table.
protocol.timed_interval: wall clock of one CREATE INDEX statement; DROP INDEX after each sample; load time recorded separately and not mixed into build_s
protocol.order_balance: Sequential A-then-B repetition, not a counterbalanced design: every pair runs stn4_multi first and stn3_single second. Order, cache, thermal and time-varying load effects can therefore bias the ratio in one direction. Earlier wording implying controlled interleaving was too strong.

stn4_multi.create_index_sql: CREATE INDEX idx ON documents USING stannum (title, body)

stn3_single.create_index_sql: CREATE INDEX idx ON documents USING stannum (concat)

field_count_shape.note: Same corpus, COPY load, CREATE INDEX wall clock only. title is fewer tokens than title+body; title+body+id adds the PK column. Compares field cardinality of the AM, not an iso-token experiment.

rows.create_index_sql: CREATE INDEX idx ON documents USING stannum (title, body)

median_ratios.interpretation: (title) is ~17× cheaper than (title, body) because title carries far fewer tokens, not because each extra field costs a constant. Adding id as a third column is a modest ~1.07× over (title, body) at the median (1.237s / 1.155s). The English multi-vs-single ~1.85× is therefore not explained by a large per-field superlinear jump at 3 columns; 2 vs 1 column on this corpus is dominated by indexing body.

insert_vs_copy.note: Isolates whether heap populated by INSERT vs COPY changes subsequent stn4_multi CREATE INDEX cost. Load time is recorded separately; only CREATE INDEX is compared. INSERT path: COPY into TEMP staging, then INSERT INTO documents SELECT (so the heap is INSERT-built, not COPY-built). This is a cheap stand-in for 'isolate FCH1 directory write from load cost'; it does not instrument FCH1 bytes directly.
insert_vs_copy.create_index_sql: CREATE INDEX idx ON documents USING stannum (title, body)
insert_vs_copy.interpretation: INSERT-built heap vs COPY-built heap did not appear to explain the observed build delta under these samples (index-after-insert median ~0.997x of index-after-copy). This is not a matched counterbalanced experiment and the FCH1 write path is still uninstrumented, so the heap load path is not exonerated either.

blocked_diagnostics.why: Did not instrument FCH1 directory write at the byte or code-path level. Used COPY vs INSERT heap population instead; CREATE INDEX cost was unchanged. No numbers invented for FCH1 write time.

conclusion_basis: Pre-declared decision rule (explicit criteria, no post-hoc tuning): (a) 'stable miss' requires median pairwise ratio > 1.8 AND at least 11 of the pairs above 1.8 AND the pair band (min..max) entirely above 1.8; (b) 'measurement noise' requires median pairwise ratio <= 1.8, which would place the C.2 single-shot 1.8689x in the tail of this profile; (c) otherwise 'inconclusive'. Measured: median 1.8451x, 9 of 12 pairs above 1.8, band 1.3401-1.9392x. Criterion (a) fails on two of its three clauses (only 9/12, band crosses 1.8), criterion (b) fails on the median, so the result is clause (c) inconclusive. The earlier wording 'almost every pair' was undefined and would have allowed either label; it is replaced by the numeric criteria above. This file must not be used to flip C.2.
conclusion_detail: N=12 interleaved pairs on a loaded M2 (loadavg ~5-7; FlClash/RepoPrompt/WindowServer each ~50% CPU). System medians match C.2's single shots to ~1% (multi 1.1360s vs 1.1451s; single 0.6123s vs 0.6127s). Median pairwise ratio is 1.8451x, so the C.2 single-shot 1.8689x sits near the middle of this profile rather than in its tail. 9 of 12 pairs are above the 1.8x ceiling. Below-ceiling pairs: pair 4 (1.7296x, a fast multi) and pairs 11-12 (1.5334x / 1.3401x) where the single-field baseline slowed to 0.7507s / 0.9530s. Correction to an earlier revision: only pair 12 shows the load spike (1-min loadavg 7.0605); pair 11's recorded loadavg_after is 5.0640, identical to pair 10's, so pair 11's slow single-field baseline is NOT explained by a recorded load event and is reported as unexplained. Interpretation guardrails: the differential is not attributable to one isolated slow multi-column CREATE INDEX, but it is also not a gap that every paired run clears, and this experiment does not separate representation cost from corpus shape, separate-column processing, or the uninstrumented FCH1 write path. Ordinary machine-load variation, concentrated in the single-column denominator, is still present in these numbers. This profile must not flip C.2.

sensitivity_excluding_load_spike_pairs_1.note: Labeled sensitivity only, not a rerun and not a second gate. Excluding pairs 11 and 12 (pair 12 shows the 1-min loadavg 7.0605 spike; pair 11 is an unexplained slow single-field baseline with loadavg_after 5.0640, i.e. not load-attributable) the median pairwise ratio is 1.8675x and 9 of 10 pairs still exceed 1.8x. Dropping samples does not move the ratio across the ceiling and must not be read as a pass.

human_label: Typical miss; single-shot threshold crossing remains underdetermined. Machine-readable `conclusion` stays `inconclusive` because the ratio band straddles the ceiling.
escalation_claim: Approved escalation wording (narrower than an earlier draft that said 'stable property of the representation'): the profile shows a repeatable end-to-end build differential for this corpus and machine. It is consistent with the cost of STN4's per-field posting representation, including its FCH1-related work, but does not establish corpus-independent behaviour, does not isolate the FCH1 contribution, and does not make the one-shot 1.8x crossing deterministic.
prior_authorization: Bounded diagnostic authorized by the user in-session on 2026-10-04 (controller ask_user after the RED C.2), selecting the design §9 'profile before inventing a second representation' option. Protocol constraints fixed before any measurement: diagnostic attachment only, never a gate rerun, never a threshold change, Phase D does not start.
